summary: The URL Standard is the living specification from the web standards community that defines URLs, domains, IP addresses, the form encoding format and their programming interface. It covers well the exact steps for reading text as an address, including resolving a relative reference against a base address, and for writing an address back out. It describes addresses rather than the content they point to, and it declares out of scope how a browser address bar turns typed input into an address. A standards audience should note that programs that are not web browsers need only implement the basic parser, and that the document is a living standard that changes over time rather than a numbered edition.

coverage.note: Model-based object tracking is outside the standard's purpose: sensing the real world is a device and runtime concern, unrelated to address syntax.
